The first tagged build of the KnightLoader Android app.

## ✨ Added

- **Find on this network** - the app sweeps its own subnet and fills in the address of anything answering as a KnightLoader, so nobody has to know an IP. It probes through a pool rather than all at once: Android queues past 64 concurrent requests, and firing all 253 off together meant everything past the first batch timed out while still waiting for a slot, never sent. A server anywhere in a typical DHCP range was simply never found.
- **QR pairing** - scanning the code on an instance's Access tab fills in the name and the address.
- **Relay-only codes are recognised** rather than mistaken for an address. Two instances can now pair through a relay, and such a code carries no address at all: the app says what the code is for and points at the relay screen, instead of dropping the whole base64 blob into the address field.
- **Relay** - reach an instance that has no path to the phone at all, by meeting it on a relay you host yourself.
- **42 languages**, following the device's own setting by default, with flags in the picker and right-to-left included.
- **Landing in the app first**, with badges for the connect screen and the settings rather than a connection form before anything else.
- **The look follows the instance you are connected to** - accent, corner shape and the rainbow mode - so the app and that instance's web interface are one product rather than two opinions. Everything can be overridden locally for anyone who wants a different colour on their own phone, and a single tap puts it back. Before any connection exists it opens in Sunflower gold, the same colour every app in the family starts from.
- **Problems?** in the settings: the version, the platform and the shape of the configuration, shareable in one tap or opened as a prefilled report. No address and no token is in it.

## 🐛 Fixed

- The address field no longer receives the pairing code itself. The Access tab carries two different QR shapes, and only one of them is a bare address.
- The app icon is the square one, drawn as a real adaptive icon: the glyph and its ground are separate layers, so no launcher mask crops it and no dark box appears behind it.

## 📋 Notes

- **This APK is signed with KnightLoader's own key**, held as a repository secret and never committed. Earlier builds of this version were signed with the Android debug key the Expo template ships (`CN=Android Debug`, public and identical for everyone), which anybody can sign an update with. If you installed one of those, uninstall it before installing this: Android identifies an app by its package name together with its signing certificate, so to a phone these are two different apps and the older one cannot be updated in place. This is the only time that will be true.
- **`versionCode` is now set explicitly.** Every build before this one was `versionCode 1`, which is what Android decides upgrade order by, so two different builds were indistinguishable to the phone.
